## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

## User impact
Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

## Minimal End-to-End Slice
- **Code**: No runtime code beyond doc-snippet consistency checks.
- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.
- **Observability**: Document how to confirm visibility behavior in the browser demo.

## Existing implementation to reuse
- Gym SLL sections in `example-games/gym/README.md`
- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

## Acceptance Criteria
- Docs explain which mode shows which chrome.
- Docs explain how to register objects as shell-owned or scene-owned.
- Docs mention that Scene-only suppresses shared shell chrome.
- Documentation changes match the implemented behavior.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Gym scene wiring (CG-0MPFM2MM4003OPP8).
- Parent: Suppress shared Gym help chrome in pure scene-only SLL views (CG-0MPFLM5EB009N5X8).

Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

## Summary

Add the episode **beat-sheet and objective layer**: a game-agnostic `createEpisodeRunner` that walks an episode manifest (acts -> scenes -> beats), charges a per-scene clock budget, classifies each scene close as `success` / `partial` / `failure`, routes to the next beat/scene from ordered, total outcome rules, and records a loss ledger. This is the build epic's core capability and the one the GDD's core loop is written against.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §1.3 core loop and §1.4 worked walkthrough (act entry -> scene outcome).
- §2.2 scene beat-sheet data model and §2.3 outcome -> next-beat selection.
- §2.4 runtime composition around the one `@story-line` choice model.
- §2.10 tension/pacing (scene budgets, refusals, failure routes) and §3.1 presentation (banner, objective, clock, ledger, restart data all read from it).
- Appendix A worked manifest (5 scenes, 15 beats, 4 endings) is the acceptance fixture.

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/compile.ts` compiles a single card's options; `src/story-line/resolve.ts` resolves one chosen option. Neither knows a scene, an objective, a budget or a route.
- The `src/story-line/` module set (`compile`, `resolve`, `resources`, `journal`, `validate`, `ui-adapter`, `types`) has no episode/manifest type; the closest artefact, `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts`, is a flat graph view model for authoring, not a run-time beat sheet.
- The spike's clock and act bookkeeping live in a game rule module (`example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts`), not in the engine.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Large** (1-3 weeks): the nearest precedent is `src/story-line/` itself (compile + resolve + resources + journal + ui-adapter + validate), which took a comparable band to establish.
- Secondary precedents: `src/ui/PhaseManager.ts` (game-agnostic phase state machine) for the clock/outcome state, and `src/core-engine/SaveLoadStore.ts` + `serializeWithVersion` for the versioned run state.
- Band is large because it is a new runtime layer plus save/load, transcript, replay and guard integration, not a helper.

## Proposed shape

- `EpisodeManifest` / `Act` / `Scene` / `Beat` / `Objective` / `OutcomeRule` / `SceneRoute` / `LossRule` types (per GDD §2.2).
- `createEpisodeRunner({ manifest, storyline, content, clock, ledger })` calling only public `@story-line` surface (GDD §2.4).
- Totality: every scene's routes cover `success` / `partial` / `failure` or end with `on: "*"`; the last rule is unconditional.
- Versioned run state: scene id, current beat card id, scene clock, scene history, route history, loss ledger.
- Unit tests over the worked manifest in GDD Appendix A (scene exits, refusals, reset ending, loss clamping).

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G1 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Add the **episode manifest schema and validator** for the story-line beat-sheet layer: `schemas/episode-manifest.schema.json`, a pure `validateEpisodeManifest(...)` implementing the GDD §2.4 rule table, and a `npm run storylines:manifest -- --manifest <file> --json` CLI. The manifest's `resources` block gains `start` and `bounds`, so gate reachability becomes provable from declared data instead of the `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` game constant.

## Problem statement

The beat-sheet data model (acts → scenes → beats → objectives, budgets, outcome rules, routes, loss rules) is specified in GDD §2.2 but cannot be checked: `schemas/` describes only the flat story-line graph, `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` builds that graph view model, and `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` validates CSV rows only — none of them knows an act, scene, beat, objective, budget or route. A designer can therefore author a manifest whose ids do not resolve, whose routes are not total, or whose declared resources disagree with the content file, and no tool refuses it. Separately, the run's starting bag lives as a game constant (`DEFAULT_RESOURCES` in `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts`), so no validator can prove from declared data that a gate is reachable.

## Users

- **Designer** (authors the manifest): "I want `storylines:manifest` to name the exact `scene`/`route`/`field` that breaks a rule, so I never ship a scene without a door."
- **Writer** (authors the CSV, never the manifest): "I want a manifest that disagrees with my content — an unknown card id, an unassigned choice card, a stale `clockCost` — to fail loudly at review time instead of at play time."
- **Build-epic implementer** (`CG-0MWR0BAT30015DPQ`): "I want the manifest shape and its validator to exist as pure, tested data seams, so `createEpisodeRunner` consumes validated input rather than re-checking it."
- **Producer/reviewer**: "I want the GDD Appendix A worked manifest to validate clean in the unit suite, so the specification cannot drift from the tooling."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `schemas/episode-manifest.schema.json` exists, validates the GDD Appendix A worked manifest under ajv in the unit suite, and models the full §2.2.1–§2.2.8 shape: `resources.{declared,irreversible,start,bounds}`, `start`, `endings`, `acts[].scenes[].{objective,budget,entryBeat,beats,outcomeRules,routes,losses}`, and `additionalProperties: false` at every level.
2. `validateEpisodeManifest(manifest, contentCards, declaredResources)` is a pure function that never throws and returns every §2.4 rule code with a machine-readable JSON path per finding: `duplicate-act`, `duplicate-scene`, `duplicate-beat`, `unknown-card`, `unknown-scene`, `unknown-act`, `unassigned-card`, `dangling-chain`, `non-total-routes`, `non-total-outcome-rules`, `objective-invalid`, `loss-not-irreversible`, `numeric-invalid`, `resource-set-mismatch`, `clock-cost-mismatch`, `ending-successor`.
3. Each rule has at least one failing unit fixture that reports exactly that code (and a clean control that reports none), and the GDD Appendix A manifest reports zero findings against `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure.csv`.
4. `npm run storylines:manifest -- --manifest <file> --json` exits `0` on a clean manifest and non-zero otherwise, emitting a stable JSON report (`code`, `path`, `message`, manifest id) plus a human-readable text report; `--help` documents the flags.
5. `resources.start` and `resources.bounds` are read from the manifest — the validator/closest reader never falls back to the game constant `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` — and the validator rejects structural inconsistency between them and `resources.declared` (missing start/bounds entry, `bounds.min > bounds.max`, `start` outside `bounds`).
6. `clock-cost-mismatch` is enforced against the legacy CSV `clockCost` cell while that column exists (G10 retires it), and is covered by a fixture that disagrees by one tick.
7. `docs/DEVELOPER.md` lists `storylines:manifest` with its flags in the story-line CLI table, and GDD §5.2 records the named check as delivered; code comments state the determinism contract (no timestamps, stable ordering).
8. `npm run build` and the unit test profile are green.

## Impact

A designer can validate an episode manifest — acts, scenes, beats, objectives, budgets and routes — with one command and get the exact broken path back, so a scene can no longer ship without a door and the run's starting bag and bounds become declared data rather than a hard-coded game constant.

## Constraints

- **Pure data + pure validator.** Reuse the `schemas/*.schema.json` + never-throwing validator pattern established by `story-line-manifest.schema.json` and `content/validate.ts`; no Phaser, no game import, no runtime layer.
- **Determinism.** No timestamps, no RNG, stable finding ordering (by path) so the report is byte-comparable.
- **Composition contract (GDD §2.1).** The manifest validator must not re-implement `@story-line`: no option parsing, no successor resolution, no prose reading, no resource arithmetic. It reads card ids/successors/declared keys from content, and beats' `clockCost` from the legacy CSV column only for the migration rule.
- **No second condition vocabulary.** `objective.check` and `SceneCondition` reuse the `{field, op, value}` shape with operators `>= <= > < ==`.
- **Out of scope:** the deterministic serialiser and `--check` drift mode (a later follow-up; this item only keeps the door open by emitting no timestamps), scene-space guard (`CG-0MWR0BG9H007AFNU`), runtime bounds clamping/spill (`CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X`), retiring the legacy columns (`CG-0MWR0BJXI007UINE`), and the runner (`CG-0MWR0BAT30015DPQ`).

## Existing state

- `schemas/` has only `story-line-manifest.schema.json` (flat graph: `nodes`, `edges`, `cycles`).
- `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — deterministic graph view-model builder, ajv-validated, `--check`-guarded via `content/artefacts.ts`.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — `validateContentCsv` / `validateContentCards`, row/column diagnostics, codes like `unknown-successor`, `unknown-resource-key`.
- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — `parseCsv`, `parseResourceDeclaration` (`#resources:` line form), `cardsFromCsv`, `compileContentOptions`.
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — `DEFAULT_RESOURCE_KEYS`, `parseResourceKeys`, `createResourceProjection`.
- `package.json` — `storylines:validate|guard|graph|author|editor|ip-scan`; no `storylines:manifest`.
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure.csv` — the spike content; per-row `resources` and legacy `act` / `clockCost` columns still present; every card id in Appendix A resolves there.
- `ajv` `^8.12.0` is already a dev dependency; no manifest CLI (`scripts/storyline-manifest.ts`) exists.

## Desired change

1. `schemas/episode-manifest.schema.json` describing the §2.2.1–§2.2.8 shape, including `resources.start` (one value per declared key) and `resources.bounds` (per-key `{min,max}`), with `additionalProperties: false` and the `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` id pattern.
2. `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — `EpisodeManifest`/`Act`/`Scene`/`Beat`/`Objective`/`OutcomeRule`/`SceneRoute`/`LossRule` types (mirroring GDD §2.2.9), `MANIFEST_VERSION`, the schema path constant, `validateEpisodeManifest`, and text/JSON report formatters in the shape used by `content/validate.ts`.
3. `scripts/storyline-manifest.ts` — `--manifest <file>` (repeatable or single with a documented default), `--json`, `--help`; resolves the content adapter from `manifest.content.adapter`, loads the CSV, and exits non-zero on any finding.
4. Barrel exports in `src/story-line/content/index.ts` (and the `@story-line` surface if the types belong there).
5. Committed fixture(s) under `tests/story-line/content/` (or `tests/fixtures/`): the Appendix A manifest plus one minimal manifest per rule; a test asserts the GDD Appendix A block and the committed fixture agree so the doc cannot drift from the validator.
6. Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` CLI table/row and story-line reference section; GDD §5.2 named-check row updated to delivered; GDD §2.2.1 `resources` row and §2.8.6 item 2 marked delivered.

**Key Files:**

- `schemas/episode-manifest.schema.json` — New schema: episode/act/scene/beat/objective/route/loss shape + `resources.start` / `resources.bounds`.
- `src/story-line/content/episode-manifest.ts` — New pure validator, types, schema path, JSON/text report formatters.
- `src/story-line/content/index.ts` — Barrel exports for the new module.
- `src/story-line/resources.ts` — Read-through for start/bounds data (no `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` fallback on the manifest path).
- `scripts/storyline-manifest.ts` — New CLI (`storylines:manifest`), JSON + text output, non-zero exit on findings.
- `package.json` — `"storylines:manifest": "tsx scripts/storyline-manifest.ts"`.
- `tests/story-line/content/episode-manifest.test.ts` — One fixture per rule + clean Appendix A case + schema-validity test.
- `tests/story-line/content/episode-manifest-cli.test.ts` — CLI exit codes and JSON shape.
- `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json` — Committed Appendix A manifest (the clean real-world target).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — CLI docs and GDD rows marked delivered.

## Related work

- `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` — **GDD engine-gap backlog** (source of this entry, G2).
- `CG-0MWR0BAT30015DPQ` — **G1 episode beat-sheet/runner epic**; blocked by this item (consumes the validated manifest).
- `CG-0MWR0BG9H007AFNU` — **G3 scene-space guard**; blocked by this item (needs `--manifest` input).
- `CG-0MWR0BJXI007UINE` — **G10 retire legacy `act`/`clockCost` columns**; blocked by this item (removes the `clock-cost-mismatch` target).
- `CG-0MWPY25W4002UNKB` — GDD foundation: setting, loop and beat-sheet data model (completed).
- `CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF` — GDD: full story-line game, Approach C (completed).
- `CG-0MWQYDC7D003G4ON` — declared resource set once per file (delivered; supplies `resources.declared` read path).
- `CG-0MWSJ8RJM001IRCJ` — spin-off discovered from this item's preparation (Gym "Public Investment" cost).
- Also touched by G1's dependencies: `CG-0MWR0BGVG004UE7X` (G4 resource bounds, a sibling of the `bounds` schema field).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the CLI validates a *manifest file against a content file*, taking `manifest.content.{adapter,file}` as the source of truth; no new registry is introduced. Reversible if the build epic prefers an explicit `--content` flag (it will be additive).
- **Assumption:** `resources.bounds` uses `{min,max}` per key; `resources.start` is one value per declared key. Both required when `resources.start` is present, so a partial block cannot silently degrade to the game constant.
- **Assumption:** `--check` drift mode and a deterministic serialiser are out of scope (the description scopes them "later"); the validator still emits no timestamps so adding it is additive.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the rule table invites extra semantic checks (clock arithmetic, reachability). Gate reachability is G3's job; only the *structural* start/bounds checks above are in scope here.
- **Risk (doc drift):** Appendix A is prose in a 3,000-line GDD; a fixture-pins-the-doc test is the mitigation.
- **Risk (legacy column):** `clock-cost-mismatch` becomes dead code once G10 lands; the rule is documented as migration-only and G10 is recorded as the removal trigger.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Does intake need to interview the producer for this item?" — Answer (agent, seed context): no. The GDD §2.2/§2.4/§2.8.6/§5.2 sections specify the typed shape, the complete rule table and the named check; the work item already names the Key Files and the effort precedent. Source: `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md`, `wl show CG-0MWR0BFMW003856N`.
- Q: "Is the deterministic serialiser + `--check` drift guard in scope?" — Answer (agent, from the item description): no — the description says "so a `--check` drift guard is possible **later**". Recorded as an explicit out-of-scope constraint. Source: work-item description, "Proposed shape".
- Q: "Where does the clean Appendix A manifest live — test fixture only, or a committed gameplay-adjacent data file?" — Answer (agent, conservative assumption): commit it as `example-games/gym/content/long-erasure-episode.json` and have the test assert the GDD block matches it, so the spec, the fixture and the tool cannot drift. Source: GDD §5.3 self-check.
- Q: "Where do `resources.start` / `resources.bounds` values come from at runtime?" — Answer (agent): the manifest; the Gym game's `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` constant is not read on the validator path. Retrofitting the game to consume the manifest is G1's scope. Source: GDD §2.8.6 item 2, §2.8.2 table.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S** – Storyline content and authoring toolchain generalised into core (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — matched: 0mwnfvlyt003m7xf, 0mwpy25w4002unkb, 0mwpy2ece002p2nh, 0mwqydc7d003g4on, 0mwr0bat30015dpq (+418 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, act, acts, adapter, add (+388 more)
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — matched: act, acts, adapter, add, additive (+334 more)

## Summary

Extend the authored-content route-space guard with a **scene-space mode** (`storylines:guard --manifest <file>`) that enumerates scene exits and beat refusals, and asserts two invariants: no exhausted close classifies as `success`, and no refusal leads to a state with no reachable ending.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.4 third static check (the clock is not a declared resource, so the content guard cannot see it).
- §2.8.6 item 5 (prove no scene exit strands the player) and §2.8 hull row (hull-costing doors stay survivable).
- §2.10 T3/T5 pacing evidence: a refusal or a hidden gate must never strand or silently truncate a run.
- §5.2 scene-space guard (named build-epic check).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` enumerates the playable route space of the **card chain** over declared resources (`gated-branch-survivable`, `ending-reachable`, `consequential-rejoin`).
- It has no manifest input, no scene boundary, no clock and no outcome/route semantics; the clock is not a declared resource, so a budget exhaustion is invisible to it.
- Bounds and clamping (G4) do not exist either, so a loss that clamps would currently enumerate differently from the authored intent.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Medium** (2-5 days): the nearest precedent is `src/story-line/content/guard.ts` itself (955 lines of bounded DFS with fail-closed truncation reporting) — this entry extends its state model with scene/clock/outcome, reusing its bound and reporting machinery.
- Band is medium because the enumeration machinery exists; the new work is state shape and the two invariants.

## Proposed shape

- Add a `--manifest` mode to `scripts/storyline-guard.ts`; keep the existing CSV mode unchanged.
- Enumerate (scene, beat, clock remaining, resources, outcome rules applied) states with the existing depth/state bounds; a bound hit stays a failure.
- Report per invariant, per scene exit and per refusal, in the existing JSON shape.
- Positive control required: a fixture whose exhausted close classifies `success` and a fixture whose refusal strands the player must both fail.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G3 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

## Summary

Give the declared resource set **bounds**: per-key min/max, spill at the maximum, clamped loss at the minimum, and a reported remainder. Deltas are applied through the declared projection, so every game with more than the `coins` / `reputation` pair gets the same guarantee.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.8 resource model: the ranges table (`hull` 0-5, `morale` 0-8, `stores` 0-6, `goodwill` 0-5, `charge` 1-2), the "surplus spills, loss clamps" behaviour and the failure state per key.
- §2.10 tension design (a clamped loss at zero must be recorded, not silently ignored).
- §2.8.6 item 1 (bounds and clamping are named gaps) and item 2 (bounds become manifest data, owned with G2).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `createResourceProjection(...).applyResourceDelta` in `src/story-line/resources.ts` forwards every finite, non-zero delta to the game's field mutator with no bounds: a gain past a cap banks, a loss below zero goes negative, and nothing is reported.
- `DEFAULT_RESOURCES` (same module) is a value bag, not a bounds declaration.
- The nearest constrained-resource helper, `src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, is hard-coded to `coins` / `reputation` and exposes only `minCoins` / `minReputation` (no maximum, no spill, no clamped-loss record).

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small-medium** (1-3 days): the nearest precedent is `src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts` (constraint-checked deltas) and the `StorylineResourceProjection` seam in `src/story-line/resources.ts`.
- Band is small-medium because the seam and its tests exist; the work is a bounds type, clamp/spill arithmetic, a reported remainder and propagation through the GDD's manifest data (G2).

## Proposed shape

- `StorylineResourceBounds = Readonly<Record<key, { min: number; max: number }>>`.
- `applyResourceDelta` returns (or reports through a callback) `{ applied, spilled, clamped }` per key; never silently discards.
- Absent bounds keep today's unbounded behaviour, so no existing game changes.
- Unit tests: spill at max, clamp at min, multi-key delta ordering, absent bounds backward compatibility.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G4 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.

data.description:
## Summary

Make **irreversibility** an engine guarantee: a declared irreversible resource key can never be granted by an option `#extra` or a manifest loss rule, and the refusal is a hard authoring error, not an authoring convention.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.8 `hull` as the irreversible tension dial (0-5, no recovery within a run).
- §2.10 irreversible-loss tension and the reset ending's structural recovery.
- §2.8.6 item 6 (`#extra=hull:1` is legal content today).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `resources.irreversible` is manifest data read only by the proposed manifest validator rule `loss-not-irreversible` (GDD §2.4); the manifest validator itself does not exist (G2).
- Nothing in `src/story-line/resources.ts` knows the concept: `selectDeclaredDelta` filters undeclared keys only (`ignored`), so a grant to a declared irreversible key is applied.
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` refuses `unknown-resource-key` (a key outside the declared set) but cannot refuse a *direction* on a declared key.
- The GDD's guard is a fixture test plus authoring discipline (GDD §2.8.3/§2.8.6), which is the gap this entry closes.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is the `unknown-resource-key` rule in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` (a declarative, row + column + reason diagnostic) plus the `selectDeclaredDelta` sign handling in `src/story-line/resources.ts`.
- Band is small because it is one declaration, one validation rule and one guard in the projection.

## Proposed shape

- Declare irreversible keys alongside the declared set (`StorylineResourceProjection` option or manifest data).
- Reject a positive delta to an irreversible key at authoring time (validator code, e.g. `irreversible-grant`) and at resolution time (refuse, log).
- Unit tests: a `#extra=hull:1` row fails validation with the row/column reason; a negative hull cost still applies.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G5 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.
data.title: Engine gap: irreversible-resource policy

data.description:
## Summary

**Surface affordability** instead of deleting it: compile an unaffordable option into a requirement object (which keys, how much is needed, how much the player has) so a presenting layer can render it disabled with its shortfall, rather than omitting it at draw time.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.3/§2.9 "an unaffordable option is not shown" — the presentation contract must say why.
- §2.8.6 item 3 (measured cost: 32 of 302 option instances hidden; 107 of 197 dead turns gate-collapsed).
- §3.6 B4 affordability presentation; §2.10 T5 (hidden affordability is not tension).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `isOptionAffordable(option, resources, declaredResources)` in `src/story-line/compile.ts` returns a boolean.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` filters unaffordable options out of `compiledOptions` at draw time, so the presenting layer never sees them; there is no requirement/shortfall shape anywhere in the compiled option model.
- `StorylineOption` (in `src/story-line/types.ts`) carries the `cost` declaration but no computed affordability state.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is `isOptionAffordable` itself plus the compiled-option shape in `src/story-line/compile.ts`; the arithmetic exists, only the output shape changes.
- Band is small because it is an additive field on the compiled option and a policy switch (omit vs surface), with no new evaluator.

## Proposed shape

- `OptionAffordability = { affordable: true } | { affordable: false; shortfall: Array<{ key; required; available }> }`.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent` gains a policy option (`'omit'` default, preserving every current caller and test; `'surface'` keeps the option with its affordability state).
- Resolution still refuses an unaffordable option (unchanged), so surfacing cannot create an illegal play path.
- Unit tests: default policy unchanged; surface policy yields the shortfall per key; an unaffordable surfaced option cannot resolve.

## Source

Discovered from `CG-0MWPY2ECE002P2NH` (GDD engine-gap backlog), entry G7 in `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §6.
data.title: Engine gap: surfaced affordability (option requirement objects)

data.description:
## Summary

Add a **resource HUD component** that renders a game-declared resource set (values, labels, max/remaining, and the loss-bearing/irreversible subset) from the declared projection, so a five-key economy is legible in play without a bespoke per-game widget.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.8.6 item 7 (where the trade is *seen*) and §2.8 each key's failure/visibility column.
- §3.1 presentation surfaces (the `resources` / status zone) and §3.4.3 colour-independent signalling for the loss-bearing key.
- §2.10 the five-key economy is a v1 requirement; H7 (can a player name what each key protects) is unproven without it.

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/ui/index.ts` exports card/hand/pile components (`HandView`, `PileView`, `TokenPileView`), `HintBar`, panels and overlays, but no component that renders a declared resource bag.
- SLL itself is not the gap: `src/ui/screen-layout.ts` resolves any zone name a game's layout declares, so a `resources` zone is layout data.
- The engine seam that would feed such a component exists (`StorylineResourceProjection.getResources` in `src/story-line/resources.ts`); the presenter does not.
- The spike renders its two-key economy with bespoke scene text; no shared component was extracted.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Medium** (2-5 days): the nearest precedents are `src/ui/TokenPileView.ts` (token stack with live count labels and click handling) and `src/ui/HintBar.ts` (compact multi-item status strip), both with SLL-positioned layouts and unit tests.
- Band is medium because it is a reusable component with layout options, labels, reduced-motion-safe updates and a loss/irreversible marker (colour plus a printed channel).

## Proposed shape

- `ResourceHud` (or `ResourceBar`) taking `{ resources, declaredKeys, bounds?, irreversible?, labels?, onChange }`.
- Value update animation respects `getEffectiveReducedMotion()`; SFX through the injected `SoundManager` using a `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` entry.
- Marker for a loss-bearing/irreversible key uses a printed channel, never colour alone.
- Unit tests: label/order/value rendering from a projection; spill/clamp display; reduced-motion path.

## Source

## Summary

Add **act/scene transition presentation**: a scene-exit banner (act title, scene title, objective result) and a sequenced act transition (banner -> objective outcome -> route) with a reduced-motion fallback. The camera-level transition helper already ships; the banner surface and the sequence do not.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.3 step D (scene close -> next beat) and §3.1 `sceneBanner` zone.
- §3.6 B5 act/scene transition presentation; §3.2 overlay/sequence behaviour.
- §2.10 pacing: the exit is where the player reads what the scene cost them.
- §3.3 audio mapping for the act/scene transition SFX.

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/ui/sceneTransition.ts` already provides `runSceneTransition` (camera fade/slide with a reduced-motion skip) — so a camera transition is **not** the gap.
- What does not exist: any banner/act-title presentation surface, any sequence that presents the scene outcome before routing, and any rendered precedent for a scene boundary. The spike has no scene boundary (`example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts`) and its layout declares six zones with no `sceneBanner` (`example-games/gym/layouts/gym-long-erasure.layout.json`: `statusBar, narrative, options, feedback, journal, controls`).
- No component in `src/ui/index.ts` composes a title + outcome + advance into a timed surface; `runSceneTransition` animates the camera only and resolves a promise.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small-medium** (1-3 days): the nearest precedents are `src/ui/sceneTransition.ts` (timed transition with reduced-motion fallback), `src/ui/narration-reveal.ts` (sequenced animated text with SFX and a skip path) and `src/ui/Overlay.ts` (`createOverlayBackground` / `dismissOverlay` depth conventions).
- Band is small-medium because every primitive exists; the work is composition, SLL zone wiring, SFX and a reduced-motion path.

## Proposed shape

- `presentSceneExit(scene, { actTitle, sceneTitle, outcome, route, reducedMotion, soundManager })` resolving when the banner is dismissed (auto-advance or click).
- Reduced motion: no slide/fade, a single immediate state with the same information.
- Outcome text and colour-independent channel (printed `success` / `partial` / `failure` word), never colour alone.
- Unit/browser tests: sequence order, skip path, reduced-motion path, SFX key selection from `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`.

## Summary

Retire the legacy **`act` / `clockCost` CSV columns** now that act membership and pacing are beat-sheet data: remove them from the Gym content adapter, migrate the remaining rows, and add the migration check that refuses a disagreeing manifest/CSV pair while both exist.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §2.1 composition contract (act membership is `scene.id`; pacing is `beat.clockCost` in the manifest).
- §2.9 "the two retired columns" and §2.4 `clock-cost-mismatch` (migration-only rule).
- §2.9.7 friction 5 (act/clock as generic `--field` writes).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` declares `act` and `clockCost` as Gym game columns and lists both in `editableColumns` (with defaults `I` / `1`), so authors can still write beat-sheet data into the wrong place.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` reads `clockCost` per beat for its pressure clock.
- The migration check (`clock-cost-mismatch`) only becomes possible once the manifest validator exists (G2), so this entry depends on it.

## Nearest precedent and effort band

- **Small** (0.5-2 days): the nearest precedent is the adapter column declaration/removal itself in `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` plus the `missing-column` diagnostic in `src/story-line/content/validate.ts`.
- Band is small because it is a content-format change with a migration, not new machinery; the validator rule is the only new logic.

## Proposed shape

- Migrate the spike's `act` / `clockCost` values into the episode manifest (Appendix A carries the same data).
- Remove both columns from the adapter and `editableColumns`; the spike's rule module reads the manifest instead.
- While both forms exist, the manifest validator rejects a disagreeing pair (`clock-cost-mismatch`); once removed, the content validator refuses the columns as unknown.
- Unit tests: CSV with the retired column fails loudly; manifest/CSV agreement passes; mismatch fails.

Add **keyboard choice navigation and overlay focus order**: number/arrow navigation of the option list with Enter/Space activation, focus traversal inside an open overlay, and Escape closing only the topmost modal — so the keyboard path in the GDD's accessibility contract is real rather than aspirational.

## Unlocks in the GDD

- §3.4.4 keyboard and touch input paths.
- §3.6 B7; §3.8 (the keyboard path is untestable until this lands).
- §3.2 overlay behaviour (exactly one modal live, Escape closes the topmost).

## Why the engine cannot do it today

- Only the panels' own toggle keys are bound: `HelpPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `FORWARD_SLASH` = `?`) and `SettingsPanel` (`toggleKey`, default `Escape`) register their own `keydown` listeners (`src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`).
- `getEndTurnKeybind()` / `setEndTurnKeybind()` in `src/ui/SettingsStore.ts` bind exactly one game action.

- Unit tests: index keys select the right option; arrow wrap; Escape closes only the topmost; disposer removes listeners.

## Goal

As a producer, I want test-generated artefacts to stay out of the working tree, so that the dev-push full-suite gate is never discarded as `state_changed_during_run` simply because a browser test produced an attachment.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` runs the full suite in the item's worktree and discards the verdict when the checkout's `git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` surface changes mid-run (`snapshot_own_checkout` / `state_changed_during_run`, SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE). Vitest 4's browser projects write `context.annotate` attachments to `<root>/.vitest-attachments/` (default `attachmentsDir`). That directory is **not** in `.gitignore`, so any run that produces an attachment (observed: the same 102 KB PNG, deterministic across two runs) leaves an untracked path behind, the fingerprint differs before/after, and the gate reports `full_suite_red` / `reason: infrastructure` — nothing is committed or pushed and the item is released to `open`.

Observed on this checkout during `CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9` (two consecutive finishes, same hash). Workaround used locally: added `.vitest-attachments/` to `.git/info/exclude` (local, untracked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.vitest-attachments/` (and any other root-level Vitest attachment output) is ignored repo-wide, either by adding it to `.gitignore` or by pinning `attachmentsDir` outside the repo in `vite.config.ts`.
- A full-suite run that produces an attachment leaves `git status --porcelain` unchanged, so `implement.py finish` is not discarded as `state_changed_during_run`.
- The chosen fix is recorded in `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (testing section) if it changes the developer workflow.

## Notes

`discovered-from:CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9`. Low risk, XS effort. The local `.git/info/exclude` workaround is not shared with other clones or CI, so this item exists to fix it at the repo level.


## Impact

A browser test that writes a Vitest attachment no longer silently discards a green full-suite verdict, so a finished change reaches `dev` instead of failing as an unexplained infrastructure red.
data.title: Ignore Vitest browser attachments so the dev-push state-change guard is not tripped
